subject: Maine's 2nd Congressional District ranked-choice tabulation
query: why is maine 2nd district going to ranked choice
title: Why is Maine's 2nd District going to ranked choice? No one passed 50%
answer: Because neither Republican Paul LePage nor Democrat Matt Dunlap won more than 50% of the votes, and Maine law then requires a ranked-choice tabulation. More than 6,000 ballots were blank in the race and 123 votes went to write-ins. The count starts Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at 10 a.m. in Augusta and usually takes about a week.
body:
Initial results reported to the Secretary of State showed LePage with 170,263 votes (49.9%) and Dunlap with 164,845 (48.3%), a gap of 5,418 votes out of just over 341,000 ballots. LePage, a former Republican governor of Maine, declared victory on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Dunlap conceded on Thursday, Nov. 5, saying, "This isn't the result we were hoping for." The tabulation still goes ahead, because it is a required step in certifying the result.

The count is held at the Maine Department of Public Safety headquarters in Augusta, is open to the public and is streamed on the Secretary of State's YouTube channel. Secretary of State Shenna Bellows said it usually takes about a week. In past runoffs most blank ballots dropped out after the first round, which Maine Public says would give LePage a majority of the remaining ballots.

Maine has used ranked-choice voting since 2018 for state and federal primaries and for federal general elections. This is the fourth time in nine years the 2nd District has needed a ranked-choice runoff; retiring Democratic Rep. Jared Golden won the three earlier ones. In the U.S. Senate race, Democrat Troy Jackson won a majority of first choices over Susan Collins, so no ranked-choice count was needed there.
in_the_news: Maine's Secretary of State will run a ranked-choice tabulation in the 2nd Congressional District starting Nov. 9, 2026, after no candidate topped 50%.
